title: Assessing the nexus of Generative AI adoption, ethical considerations and organizational performance
explain_beginner: Researchers surveyed 384 managers to understand why companies adopt artificial intelligence tools and how this affects their success. They found that companies adopt these tools because of pressure from competitors, industry standards, and colleagues, but also because of ethical concerns about fairness and honesty. Importantly, ethical principles like transparency and accountability actually encourage adoption rather than discourage it. Companies that use these tools effectively and innovate tend to perform better overall.
explain_business: Organizations considering GenAI deployment should recognize that ethical principles around fairness and transparency drive adoption rather than hinder it, making them business enablers rather than obstacles. Institutional pressures from competitors and industry peers will naturally push adoption, but performance gains depend on building organizational capacity for innovation. Executives should prioritize ethical governance frameworks alongside implementation strategies, as companies demonstrating strong ethical practices and innovation capabilities will realize greater business benefits from their GenAI investments.
explain_practitioner: This study examined GenAI adoption drivers across 384 IT and ITeS managers using institutional theory and ethical AI frameworks. PLS-SEM analysis revealed that three institutional pressures, coercive, normative and mimetic forces, significantly influence adoption. Five ethical dimensions, fairness, accountability, transparency, accuracy and autonomy, also measurably predict GenAI use. GenAI deployment positively correlates with organizational performance, with organizational innovativeness acting as a significant moderator strengthening this relationship. The findings validate a comprehensive model linking institutional and ethical factors to both adoption and performance outcomes.
